correctness.rationale: The proof derives Z_n[i]=1+nu_2(i), the exact occurrence classes, uniqueness of the maximal symbol in every factor, and valuation invariance of every centered neighborhood up to radius 2^{j-1}-1. Each factor is therefore re-centered at any occurrence of its maximum letter. This establishes the full iff without hidden boundary cases. The generating polynomial follows from independent nonempty subsets of occurrence classes; the minimum and total counts are exact coefficient evaluations. A standalone verifier compares the theorem to occurrence-mask enumeration for all 32,906 subsets through n=4 and all 33,867 minimum candidates through n=6, plus longer structural checks. Computation is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the factor-occurrence hitting sets for the canonical recursively nested Zimin words, not a mere renaming of a number sequence: it identifies every valid attractor of every cardinality via a simple iff criterion and yields the complete size-generating polynomial. The multiplicity of optimal attractors grows as 2^{n(n-1)/2}, contrasting with constant or exponential optimal-attractor counts for other natural recursive words in the primary literature. This resolves the exact attractive-position geometry for a meaningful family and is independently checkable from its factor structure; it does not claim compression algorithms or broader morphic generalizations.
